Name: layer_gating_expression
Title: The Last Gate: Layers That Decide Whether Knowledge Reaches the Output
Short Hypothesis: A specific band of late layers gates whether retrieved knowledge is expressed, applying content-general suppression under certain conditions (uncertainty, format mismatch, safety-like triggers); knowledge decodable before this gate is often not expressed after it, and modulating the gate changes expression without changing what was retrieved. This gate is the locus of many knowing-vs-saying failures.
Related Work: Refusal and behavior-gating directions have been found (e.g., a single 'refusal direction'; Arditi et al., 2024). We generalize to a factual-expression gate that governs whether retrieved knowledge surfaces, tie it to a late-layer band, and connect it to knowing-vs-saying failures beyond safety refusals-a broader expression-control mechanism.
Abstract: Retrieved knowledge does not always reach the output. We hypothesize a late-layer expression gate: a band of layers that modulates whether internally-retrieved facts are surfaced, applying content-general suppression under conditions like uncertainty or format mismatch, and functioning as a common bottleneck for knowing-vs-saying failures. We locate the gate by contrasting cases where a fact is decodable pre-gate but not expressed post-gate, and by searching for a low-rank expression-control direction in the late-layer band. We test that (i) many known-but-unsaid failures share this gate's signature; (ii) an expression direction exists whose modulation changes whether decodable facts are expressed, with limited effect on which fact is retrieved; and (iii) the gate responds to general triggers (uncertainty, atypical format) rather than specific relations. We evaluate across models and datasets, relating gate activity to expression failures and testing causal control. Establishing a factual-expression gate would unify diverse knowing-vs-saying failures under one mechanism, generalize behavior-gating findings from safety to factual expression, and provide a targeted control to release stored knowledge that is being needlessly suppressed-directly actionable for improving factual output without retraining.
Experiments: 1. Identify known-but-unsaid failures via pre-gate decodability + wrong output. 2. Localize a late-layer band and a low-rank expression direction (difference-of-means between expressed and suppressed cases). 3. Test shared gate signature across failures. 4. Modulate the expression direction; measure change in expression vs retrieval content. 5. Probe gate triggers (uncertainty, format). Metrics: gate-signature prevalence, expression-direction control effect, retrieval-content invariance, trigger correlations.
Risk Factors and Limitations: An expression direction may entangle with content, undermining the invariance claim. The gate may be several mechanisms, not one. Modulation may harm calibration or safety behaviors. Attribution to a specific layer band may be fuzzy.
